blocks.prompt: 2 (i) Express the complex number in polar form: \(4 + 3i\).
blocks.explanation: Yeh polar form ka sawal hai: humein \(z = x + iy\) ko \(r(\cos\theta + i\sin\theta)\) ki shakal mein likhna hai. Polar form asal mein point ka pata 'kitni door aur kis taraf' ki zubaan mein batata hai: r origin se faasla (modulus) hai aur \(\theta\) direction (argument). Plan: (1) x aur y ke sign se quadrant pehchanein, (2) \(r = \sqrt{x^{2} + y^{2}}\) se modulus nikaalein, (3) \(\tan^{-1}|y/x|\) se reference angle (x-axis ke saath chhota angle) lein, (4) quadrant ke mutabiq use principal argument (\(-\pi < \theta \le \pi\)) mein badlein. Yahan dono parts positive hain, is liye kaam seedha hai, lekin y/x aur x/y ka farq yaad rakhna hai: answer key ne yahin ghalti ki hai.
steps:
Given (diya gaya hai): \(z = 4 + 3i\), yani \(x = 4\) (real part), \(y = 3\) (imaginary part).
To find (maloom karna hai): modulus r aur principal argument \(\theta\), taake \(z = r(\cos\theta + i\sin\theta)\) likh sakein.
Method (tareeqa): \(r = \sqrt{x^{2}+y^{2}}\) (Pythagoras), aur \(\theta\) ke liye pehle reference angle, phir quadrant ka rule.

Quadrant pehchanein
\(x = 4 > 0\) aur \(y = 3 > 0\): point \((4, 3)\) pehle (first) quadrant mein hai.
Kyun: First quadrant mein calculator ka \(\tan^{-1}(y/x)\) hi asal argument hota hai; koi adjustment nahi chahiye. Doosre quadrants mein calculator dhoka de sakta hai, is liye hum hamesha pehle quadrant dekhte hain.

Modulus nikaalein
\[r = \sqrt{4^{2} + 3^{2}}\]
\[r = \sqrt{16 + 9} = \sqrt{25} = 5\]
Kyun: r point \((4, 3)\) ka O se faasla hai. x aur y ek right-angled triangle ki do sides hain aur r us ka hypotenuse (kaan), is liye Pythagoras lagta hai. Yeh mashhoor 3-4-5 triangle hai.

Argument nikaalein
\[\theta = \tan^{-1}\dfrac{3}{4}\]
\[\theta \approx 36.87^{\circ}\]
(radian mein \(\theta \approx 0.6435\))
Kyun: argument ke liye \(\tan\theta = \dfrac{y}{x} = \dfrac{3}{4}\) hota hai, yani 'upar ki doori' taqseem 'daayein ki doori'. \(\frac{3}{4}\) koi standard value nahi, is liye calculator se decimal angle liya.
Dhyan dein: y upar (numerator) aur x neeche (denominator) aata hai. Agar ulta \(\tan^{-1}\frac{4}{3}\) le liya to \(53.13^{\circ}\) aata hai, jo \(3 + 4i\) ka angle hai, \(4 + 3i\) ka nahi.

Polar form likhein
\[z = 5(\cos 36.87^{\circ} + i\sin 36.87^{\circ})\]
Kyun: bas r aur \(\theta\) ko \(r(\cos\theta + i\sin\theta)\) mein rakh diya.

Tasdeeq (check):
Polar form se wapas x aur y nikaal kar dekhte hain ke wohi number milta hai ya nahi:
\[5\cos 36.87^{\circ} \approx 5(0.8) = 4\]
\[5\sin 36.87^{\circ} \approx 5(0.6) = 3\]
Hamein wapas \(4 + 3i\) mil gaya, is liye jawab sahi hai.
blocks.final_answer: \(4 + 3i = 5(\cos 36.87^{\circ} + i\sin 36.87^{\circ})\), yani \(r = 5\), \(\theta = \tan^{-1}\frac{3}{4} \approx 36.87^{\circ}\) (0.6435 rad). Matlab: point O se 5 units door, polar axis se \(36.87^{\circ}\) upar hai.

blocks.title: Kitab ki ghalti
blocks.text: Answer key \(5(\cos 53.13^{\circ} + i\sin 53.13^{\circ})\) chhaapti hai. Yeh angle \(\tan^{-1}\frac{4}{3}\) hai (x aur y ulat gaye) aur is se \(3 + 4i\) banta hai, \(4 + 3i\) nahin. Sahi jawab \(5(\cos 36.87^{\circ} + i\sin 36.87^{\circ})\) hai.

blocks.prompt: 2 (ii) Express the complex number in polar form: \(1 + i\).
blocks.explanation: Yeh polar form ka sawal hai: humein \(z = x + iy\) ko \(r(\cos\theta + i\sin\theta)\) ki shakal mein likhna hai. Polar form asal mein point ka pata 'kitni door aur kis taraf' ki zubaan mein batata hai: r origin se faasla (modulus) hai aur \(\theta\) direction (argument). Plan: (1) x aur y ke sign se quadrant pehchanein, (2) \(r = \sqrt{x^{2} + y^{2}}\) se modulus nikaalein, (3) \(\tan^{-1}|y/x|\) se reference angle (x-axis ke saath chhota angle) lein, (4) quadrant ke mutabiq use principal argument (\(-\pi < \theta \le \pi\)) mein badlein. Yahan x aur y barabar hain, is liye angle ek standard angle niklega aur hum exact jawab likh sakte hain.
steps:
Given (diya gaya hai): \(z = 1 + i\), yani \(x = 1\), \(y = 1\).
To find (maloom karna hai): modulus r aur principal argument \(\theta\), taake \(z = r(\cos\theta + i\sin\theta)\) likh sakein.
Method (tareeqa): \(r = \sqrt{x^{2}+y^{2}}\) (Pythagoras), aur \(\theta\) ke liye pehle reference angle, phir quadrant ka rule.

Quadrant pehchanein
\(x > 0\), \(y > 0\): pehla (first) quadrant.
Kyun: First quadrant mein reference angle hi argument hai, koi tabdeeli nahi chahiye.

Modulus nikaalein
\[r = \sqrt{1^{2} + 1^{2}} = \sqrt{2}\]
Kyun: \((1, 1)\) ka O se faasla, Pythagoras se. \(\sqrt{2}\) ko decimal mein na badlein; exact jawab behtar hai.

Argument nikaalein
\[\theta = \tan^{-1}\dfrac{1}{1} = \tan^{-1} 1\]
\[\theta = \dfrac{\pi}{4} = 45^{\circ}\]
Kyun: \(\tan\theta = \frac{1}{1} = 1\), aur hum jaante hain ke \(\tan 45^{\circ} = 1\). Jab x aur y barabar hon to point bilkul beech wali (diagonal) line par hota hai, jo dono axes se \(45^{\circ}\) par hai.

Polar form likhein
\[z = \sqrt{2}\left(\cos\dfrac{\pi}{4} + i\sin\dfrac{\pi}{4}\right)\]
Kyun: \(r(\cos\theta + i\sin\theta)\) mein \(r = \sqrt{2}\) aur \(\theta = \frac{\pi}{4}\) rakhe.

Tasdeeq (check):
\[\sqrt{2}\cos\dfrac{\pi}{4} = \sqrt{2} \cdot \dfrac{1}{\sqrt{2}} = 1\]
aur sine wala hissa bhi isi tarah 1 deta hai, is liye wapas \(1 + i\) mil gaya.
blocks.final_answer: \(1 + i = \sqrt{2}\left(\cos\frac{\pi}{4} + i\sin\frac{\pi}{4}\right)\): O se \(\sqrt{2}\) door, \(45^{\circ}\) ki direction mein.

blocks.prompt: 2 (iii) Express the complex number in polar form: \(\frac{1}{2} + \frac{\sqrt{3}}{2}i\).
blocks.explanation: Yeh polar form ka sawal hai: humein \(z = x + iy\) ko \(r(\cos\theta + i\sin\theta)\) ki shakal mein likhna hai. Polar form asal mein point ka pata 'kitni door aur kis taraf' ki zubaan mein batata hai: r origin se faasla (modulus) hai aur \(\theta\) direction (argument). Plan: (1) x aur y ke sign se quadrant pehchanein, (2) \(r = \sqrt{x^{2} + y^{2}}\) se modulus nikaalein, (3) \(\tan^{-1}|y/x|\) se reference angle (x-axis ke saath chhota angle) lein, (4) quadrant ke mutabiq use principal argument (\(-\pi < \theta \le \pi\)) mein badlein. Yahan values \(\frac{1}{2}\) aur \(\frac{\sqrt{3}}{2}\) dekh kar hi ek achha student pehchaan leta hai ke yeh \(60^{\circ}\) ke cos aur sin hain.
steps:
Given (diya gaya hai): \(x = \frac{1}{2}\), \(y = \frac{\sqrt{3}}{2}\). Dono positive hain, is liye point pehle (first) quadrant mein hai.
To find (maloom karna hai): modulus r aur principal argument \(\theta\), taake \(z = r(\cos\theta + i\sin\theta)\) likh sakein.
Method (tareeqa): \(r = \sqrt{x^{2}+y^{2}}\) (Pythagoras), aur \(\theta\) ke liye pehle reference angle, phir quadrant ka rule.

Modulus nikaalein
\[r = \sqrt{\dfrac{1}{4} + \dfrac{3}{4}}\]
\[r = \sqrt{1} = 1\]
Kyun: \(\left(\frac{1}{2}\right)^{2} = \frac{1}{4}\) aur \(\left(\frac{\sqrt{3}}{2}\right)^{2} = \frac{3}{4}\); in ka jama 1 hai. Yani yeh point unit circle (radius 1 wala circle) par hai.

Argument nikaalein
\[\tan\theta = \dfrac{\sqrt{3}/2}{1/2} = \sqrt{3}\]
\[\theta = \dfrac{\pi}{3} = 60^{\circ}\]
Kyun: fraction ke upar aur neeche dono mein \(\frac{1}{2}\) hai jo cancel ho jata hai. \(\tan 60^{\circ} = \sqrt{3}\) yaad hai, aur point first quadrant mein hai, is liye \(\theta = 60^{\circ}\) hi sahi hai.

Polar form likhein
\[z = 1\left(\cos\dfrac{\pi}{3} + i\sin\dfrac{\pi}{3}\right)\]
Kyun: \(r = 1\) aur \(\theta = \frac{\pi}{3}\) rakh diye. r = 1 ho to use likhna zaroori nahi, lekin likhne se form wazeh rehti hai.

Tasdeeq (check):
\[\cos\dfrac{\pi}{3} = \dfrac{1}{2},\ \sin\dfrac{\pi}{3} = \dfrac{\sqrt{3}}{2}\]
jo bilkul wapas z deta hai.
blocks.final_answer: \(\frac{1}{2} + \frac{\sqrt{3}}{2}i = 1\left(\cos\frac{\pi}{3} + i\sin\frac{\pi}{3}\right)\): unit circle par \(60^{\circ}\) wala point.

blocks.prompt: 2 (iv) Express the complex number in polar form: \(-\frac{5}{2} - \frac{5\sqrt{3}}{2}i\).
blocks.explanation: Yeh polar form ka sawal hai: humein \(z = x + iy\) ko \(r(\cos\theta + i\sin\theta)\) ki shakal mein likhna hai. Polar form asal mein point ka pata 'kitni door aur kis taraf' ki zubaan mein batata hai: r origin se faasla (modulus) hai aur \(\theta\) direction (argument). Plan: (1) x aur y ke sign se quadrant pehchanein, (2) \(r = \sqrt{x^{2} + y^{2}}\) se modulus nikaalein, (3) \(\tan^{-1}|y/x|\) se reference angle (x-axis ke saath chhota angle) lein, (4) quadrant ke mutabiq use principal argument (\(-\pi < \theta \le \pi\)) mein badlein. Is part mein dono parts negative hain, yani third quadrant. Yahi woh jagah hai jahan calculator dhoka deta hai, is liye angle ko hum khud sahi quadrant mein rakhenge.
steps:
Given (diya gaya hai): \(x = -\frac{5}{2}\), \(y = -\frac{5\sqrt{3}}{2}\).
To find (maloom karna hai): modulus r aur principal argument \(\theta\), taake \(z = r(\cos\theta + i\sin\theta)\) likh sakein.
Method (tareeqa): \(r = \sqrt{x^{2}+y^{2}}\) (Pythagoras), aur \(\theta\) ke liye pehle reference angle, phir quadrant ka rule.

Quadrant pehchanein
\(x < 0\) aur \(y < 0\): teesra (third) quadrant.
Kyun: \(\frac{y}{x}\) mein dono minus cancel ho jaate hain, is liye calculator ko lagta hai ke point first quadrant mein hai. Woh do minus nahi dekh sakta; hamein khud angle ko third quadrant mein le jaana hai.

Modulus nikaalein
\[r = \sqrt{\dfrac{25}{4} + \dfrac{75}{4}}\]
\[r = \sqrt{\dfrac{100}{4}} = \sqrt{25} = 5\]
Kyun: square karne se minus sign khatam ho jata hai, kyunke faasla kabhi negative nahi hota. \(\left(\frac{5\sqrt{3}}{2}\right)^{2} = \frac{25 \times 3}{4} = \frac{75}{4}\).

Reference angle nikaalein
\[\alpha = \tan^{-1}\dfrac{5\sqrt{3}/2}{5/2} = \tan^{-1}\sqrt{3}\]
\[\alpha = \dfrac{\pi}{3}\]
Kyun: reference angle \(\alpha\) sirf x aur y ke size (bina sign) se nikalta hai; yeh x-axis ke saath bana chhota angle hai. \(\tan^{-1}\sqrt{3} = 60^{\circ} = \frac{\pi}{3}\).

Principal argument nikaalein
\[\theta = -(\pi - \alpha)\]
\[\theta = -\left(\pi - \dfrac{\pi}{3}\right) = -\dfrac{2\pi}{3}\]
Kyun: principal argument \(-\pi\) aur \(\pi\) ke darmiyan hona chahiye. Third quadrant tak pohanchne ke do raaste hain: anticlockwise \(\pi + \frac{\pi}{3} = \frac{4\pi}{3}\), ya clockwise \(-\frac{2\pi}{3}\). Dono ek hi direction hain, lekin \(\frac{4\pi}{3}\) range se bahar hai, is liye principal value \(-\frac{2\pi}{3}\) hai.
Dhyan dein: third quadrant mein principal argument hamesha negative hota hai: \(\theta = -(\pi - \alpha)\).

Polar form likhein
\[z = 5\left(\cos\left(-\dfrac{2\pi}{3}\right) + i\sin\left(-\dfrac{2\pi}{3}\right)\right)\]
Kyun: \(r(\cos\theta + i\sin\theta)\) mein principal argument rakha.

Tasdeeq (check):
\[5\cos\left(-\dfrac{2\pi}{3}\right) = 5\left(-\dfrac{1}{2}\right) = -\dfrac{5}{2}\]
\[5\sin\left(-\dfrac{2\pi}{3}\right) = -\dfrac{5\sqrt{3}}{2}\]
Dono parts z se mil gaye, is liye jawab sahi hai.
blocks.final_answer: \(z = 5\left(\cos\left(-\frac{2\pi}{3}\right) + i\sin\left(-\frac{2\pi}{3}\right)\right)\); yeh wohi number hai jo \(5\left(\cos\frac{4\pi}{3} + i\sin\frac{4\pi}{3}\right)\), jo answer key ki form hai. Dono sahi hain; principal value \(-\frac{2\pi}{3}\) hai.

blocks.prompt: 2 (v) Express the complex number in polar form: \(-\frac{5}{7} + \frac{\sqrt{8}}{7}i\).
blocks.explanation: Yeh polar form ka sawal hai: humein \(z = x + iy\) ko \(r(\cos\theta + i\sin\theta)\) ki shakal mein likhna hai. Polar form asal mein point ka pata 'kitni door aur kis taraf' ki zubaan mein batata hai: r origin se faasla (modulus) hai aur \(\theta\) direction (argument). Plan: (1) x aur y ke sign se quadrant pehchanein, (2) \(r = \sqrt{x^{2} + y^{2}}\) se modulus nikaalein, (3) \(\tan^{-1}|y/x|\) se reference angle (x-axis ke saath chhota angle) lein, (4) quadrant ke mutabiq use principal argument (\(-\pi < \theta \le \pi\)) mein badlein. Yahan x negative aur y positive hai, yani second quadrant, aur angle standard nahi, is liye decimal mein aayega.
steps:
Given (diya gaya hai): \(x = -\frac{5}{7}\), \(y = \frac{\sqrt{8}}{7}\).
To find (maloom karna hai): modulus r aur principal argument \(\theta\), taake \(z = r(\cos\theta + i\sin\theta)\) likh sakein.
Method (tareeqa): \(r = \sqrt{x^{2}+y^{2}}\) (Pythagoras), aur \(\theta\) ke liye pehle reference angle, phir quadrant ka rule.

Quadrant pehchanein
\(x < 0\), \(y > 0\): doosra (second) quadrant.
Kyun: Signs ka pattern hi batata hai ke reference angle ko kaise istemal karna hai: second quadrant mein \(\theta = \pi - \alpha\).

Modulus nikaalein
\[r = \sqrt{\dfrac{25}{49} + \dfrac{8}{49}}\]
\[r = \sqrt{\dfrac{33}{49}} = \dfrac{\sqrt{33}}{7}\]
Kyun: \(\left(\frac{\sqrt{8}}{7}\right)^{2} = \frac{8}{49}\), kyunke square root ka square wahi number deta hai. Neeche \(\sqrt{49} = 7\) bahar aa jata hai, upar \(\sqrt{33}\) aage simplify nahi hota.

Reference angle nikaalein
\[\alpha = \tan^{-1}\dfrac{\sqrt{8}}{5}\]
\[\alpha = \tan^{-1}(0.5657) \approx 29.50^{\circ}\]
Kyun: \(\frac{\sqrt{8}/7}{5/7}\) mein 7 cancel ho jate hain. \(\sqrt{8} = 2\sqrt{2} \approx 2.828\). Yeh standard angle nahi, is liye calculator se decimal lena parta hai.

Principal argument nikaalein
\[\theta = 180^{\circ} - \alpha\]
\[\theta \approx 180^{\circ} - 29.50^{\circ} = 150.50^{\circ}\]
Kyun: second quadrant mein ray negative x-axis (\(180^{\circ}\)) se \(\alpha\) kam hoti hai. \(150.50^{\circ}\) pehle hi \((-180^{\circ}, 180^{\circ}]\) mein hai, is liye yahi principal argument hai.
Dhyan dein: agar calculator mein seedha \(\tan^{-1}\left(\frac{\sqrt{8}}{-5}\right)\) daalein to \(-29.50^{\circ}\) aata hai, jo fourth quadrant hai. Yeh ghalat hai.

Polar form likhein
\[z = \dfrac{\sqrt{33}}{7}(\cos 150.50^{\circ} + i\sin 150.50^{\circ})\]
Kyun: \(r(\cos\theta + i\sin\theta)\) mein values rakhin.

Tasdeeq (check):
\[r \approx 0.8207\]
\[0.8207\cos 150.50^{\circ} \approx -0.714\]
\[0.8207\sin 150.50^{\circ} \approx 0.404\]
aur \(-\frac{5}{7} \approx -0.714\), \(\frac{\sqrt{8}}{7} \approx 0.404\). Dono mil gaye, jawab sahi hai.
blocks.final_answer: \(z = \frac{\sqrt{33}}{7}(\cos 150.50^{\circ} + i\sin 150.50^{\circ})\), jahan \(\theta = \pi - \tan^{-1}\frac{2\sqrt{2}}{5} \approx 2.627\) rad. Point O se taqreeban 0.82 door, second quadrant mein hai.

blocks.prompt: 2 (vi) Express the complex number in polar form: \(\frac{1}{2} + \frac{\sqrt{5}}{2}i\).
blocks.explanation: Yeh polar form ka sawal hai: humein \(z = x + iy\) ko \(r(\cos\theta + i\sin\theta)\) ki shakal mein likhna hai. Polar form asal mein point ka pata 'kitni door aur kis taraf' ki zubaan mein batata hai: r origin se faasla (modulus) hai aur \(\theta\) direction (argument). Plan: (1) x aur y ke sign se quadrant pehchanein, (2) \(r = \sqrt{x^{2} + y^{2}}\) se modulus nikaalein, (3) \(\tan^{-1}|y/x|\) se reference angle (x-axis ke saath chhota angle) lein, (4) quadrant ke mutabiq use principal argument (\(-\pi < \theta \le \pi\)) mein badlein. Dono parts positive hain, to first quadrant; bas modulus aur angle dhyan se nikaalne hain.
steps:
Given (diya gaya hai): \(x = \frac{1}{2}\), \(y = \frac{\sqrt{5}}{2}\). Dono positive, is liye pehla (first) quadrant.
To find (maloom karna hai): modulus r aur principal argument \(\theta\), taake \(z = r(\cos\theta + i\sin\theta)\) likh sakein.
Method (tareeqa): \(r = \sqrt{x^{2}+y^{2}}\) (Pythagoras), aur \(\theta\) ke liye pehle reference angle, phir quadrant ka rule.

Modulus nikaalein
\[r = \sqrt{\dfrac{1}{4} + \dfrac{5}{4}} = \sqrt{\dfrac{6}{4}}\]
\[r = \dfrac{\sqrt{6}}{2}\]
Kyun: \(\frac{1}{4} + \frac{5}{4} = \frac{6}{4}\), aur \(\sqrt{\frac{6}{4}} = \frac{\sqrt{6}}{\sqrt{4}}\); neeche \(\sqrt{4} = 2\) bahar aa jata hai.

Argument nikaalein
\[\theta = \tan^{-1}\dfrac{\sqrt{5}/2}{1/2} = \tan^{-1}\sqrt{5}\]
\[\theta \approx 65.91^{\circ}\]
(radian mein \(\theta \approx 1.150\))
Kyun: \(\frac{1}{2}\) upar neeche se cancel ho gaya. First quadrant hai, is liye calculator ki value hi argument hai; \(\sqrt{5} \approx 2.236\).

Polar form likhein
\[z = \dfrac{\sqrt{6}}{2}(\cos 65.91^{\circ} + i\sin 65.91^{\circ})\]
Kyun: r aur \(\theta\) form mein rakhe.

Tasdeeq (check):
\(r = \frac{\sqrt{6}}{2} \approx 1.2247\) le kar:
\[1.2247\cos 65.91^{\circ} \approx 0.500\]
\[1.2247\sin 65.91^{\circ} \approx 1.118\]
aur \(\frac{\sqrt{5}}{2} \approx 1.118\). Dono parts mil gaye.

blocks.prompt: 2 (vii) Express the complex number in polar form: \(-\frac{2}{3} - \frac{\sqrt{7}}{3}i\).
blocks.explanation: Yeh polar form ka sawal hai: humein \(z = x + iy\) ko \(r(\cos\theta + i\sin\theta)\) ki shakal mein likhna hai. Polar form asal mein point ka pata 'kitni door aur kis taraf' ki zubaan mein batata hai: r origin se faasla (modulus) hai aur \(\theta\) direction (argument). Plan: (1) x aur y ke sign se quadrant pehchanein, (2) \(r = \sqrt{x^{2} + y^{2}}\) se modulus nikaalein, (3) \(\tan^{-1}|y/x|\) se reference angle (x-axis ke saath chhota angle) lein, (4) quadrant ke mutabiq use principal argument (\(-\pi < \theta \le \pi\)) mein badlein. Is part mein dono parts negative hain, yani phir third quadrant; is liye principal argument negative aayega.
steps:
Given (diya gaya hai): \(x = -\frac{2}{3}\), \(y = -\frac{\sqrt{7}}{3}\).
To find (maloom karna hai): modulus r aur principal argument \(\theta\), taake \(z = r(\cos\theta + i\sin\theta)\) likh sakein.
Method (tareeqa): \(r = \sqrt{x^{2}+y^{2}}\) (Pythagoras), aur \(\theta\) ke liye pehle reference angle, phir quadrant ka rule.

Quadrant pehchanein
\(x < 0\), \(y < 0\): teesra (third) quadrant.
Kyun: dono signs negative hain. Calculator yeh nahi dekh sakta, is liye quadrant hum khud tay karte hain.

Modulus nikaalein
\[r = \sqrt{\dfrac{4}{9} + \dfrac{7}{9}} = \sqrt{\dfrac{11}{9}}\]
\[r = \dfrac{\sqrt{11}}{3}\]
Kyun: \(\frac{4}{9} + \frac{7}{9} = \frac{11}{9}\), aur neeche \(\sqrt{9} = 3\) bahar aata hai.

Reference angle nikaalein
\[\alpha = \tan^{-1}\dfrac{\sqrt{7}}{2}\]
\[\alpha = \tan^{-1}(1.3229) \approx 52.91^{\circ}\]
Kyun: 3 upar neeche se cancel ho gaye; \(\sqrt{7} \approx 2.6458\). Reference angle sirf sizes se nikalta hai, signs se nahi.

Principal argument nikaalein
\[\theta = -(180^{\circ} - \alpha)\]
\[\theta \approx -(180^{\circ} - 52.91^{\circ})\]
\[\theta \approx -127.09^{\circ}\]
Kyun: third quadrant mein principal argument tak clockwise jaate hain, taake \(\theta\) range \((-180^{\circ}, 180^{\circ}]\) mein rahe. Anticlockwise \(180^{\circ} + 52.91^{\circ} = 232.91^{\circ}\) bhi wohi direction hai, lekin principal value nahi.
Dhyan dein: \(-(180^{\circ} - \alpha)\) mein bracket ka minus poore bracket par lagta hai: \(-180^{\circ} + 52.91^{\circ}\).

Polar form likhein
\[z = \dfrac{\sqrt{11}}{3}(\cos(-127.09^{\circ}) + i\sin(-127.09^{\circ}))\]
Kyun: \(r(\cos\theta + i\sin\theta)\) mein values rakhin.

Tasdeeq (check):
\(r = \frac{\sqrt{11}}{3} \approx 1.1055\) le kar:
\[1.1055\cos(-127.09^{\circ}) \approx -0.667\]
\[1.1055\sin(-127.09^{\circ}) \approx -0.882\]
aur \(-\frac{2}{3} \approx -0.667\), \(-\frac{\sqrt{7}}{3} \approx -0.882\). Dono mil gaye.
